title: Irkutsk laboratory-worker death evidence tracker
question: What is publicly established about the death of a worker at an Irkutsk infectious-disease research institute, and do the available records establish plague, an occupational pathogen link, a laboratory accident, a second plague case, or a second death?
answer: A worker death and an official description of pneumonia of unknown origin are publicly reported. As of the bounded review, the causative agent, pneumonic plague diagnosis, occupational pathogen link, laboratory accident, second plague case, and second death are not established by qualifying public evidence.

evidence.title: WHO statement carried by the United Nations Geneva newsroom
evidence.publisher: United Nations Geneva / World Health Organization
evidence.supports: A female laboratory worker died; authorities were testing the cause, monitoring identified contacts, and WHO published an initial risk assessment.
evidence.does_not_establish: A causative agent, a diagnosis of pneumonic plague, an occupational pathogen link, a laboratory accident, a second plague case, or a second death.
evidence.source_date_semantics: Date displayed on the UNOG newsroom article and its press-briefing dateline; original v0.1/v0.2 records preserved.

evidence.title: WHO still did not know the causative agent in the Irkutsk death
evidence.supports: WHO said it did not know the causative agent; the Russian public-health statement described pneumonia of unknown origin and reported testing of contacts.
evidence.does_not_establish: That media speculation about plague or a laboratory accident is correct.

evidence.title: Russian public-health statement reported no evidence tying the illness to worked-with pathogens
evidence.supports: Russian authorities publicly reported pneumonia of unknown origin, no evidence of illness from pathogens handled at work, and no institute incident involving pathogenic microorganisms.
evidence.does_not_establish: An independently replicated occupational-safety investigation or a final clinical diagnosis.

evidence.title: Rospotrebnadzor commission findings reported by TASS
evidence.supports: The cited commission reported no laboratory accident and used the diagnosis description pneumonia of unknown etiology.
evidence.does_not_establish: Independent confirmation of the commission's methods or a final pathogen diagnosis.

evidence.title: Fact check of circulating Irkutsk claims
evidence.supports: The reviewed public record did not prove a laboratory accident; unrelated WHO and video material were circulating alongside the event.
evidence.does_not_establish: A final diagnosis or an independent laboratory investigation.

evidence.title: WHO plague fact sheet
evidence.supports: Plague is a bacterial disease caused by Yersinia pestis and pneumonic plague has defined clinical and public-health characteristics.
evidence.does_not_establish: That plague caused the Irkutsk worker's illness or death.
evidence.source_date_semantics: Date displayed on the WHO page in this review; original publication date is not established.

evidence.title: Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute public description
evidence.supports: The institute publicly describes work on plague and other dangerous infectious diseases.
evidence.does_not_establish: Which agent, if any, was involved in the worker's illness, or that a workplace incident occurred.

evidence.title: WHO Director-General opening remarks, 7 October 2026
evidence.supports: WHO sought laboratory-test information, reasons for public-health measures and contact health status; it sought verification of a second-employee media report and said the information was insufficient for a full risk assessment.
evidence.does_not_establish: A plague diagnosis, an occupational exposure chain, a confirmed second case or a second death.

evidence.title: Public post attributed to Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
evidence.publisher: Named public LinkedIn account attributed to Tedros
evidence.source_date_semantics: Only a relative 3h label was displayed; no absolute publication time was verified.
evidence.supports: The post dates the reported death to 2 October and relays Russian information that medical observation of all identified contacts had ended.
evidence.does_not_establish: Independently verified clinical or contact follow-up records, a confirmed pathogen, or that transmission has been excluded.

evidence.title: Reuters follow-up retained from the recovered public handoff
evidence.publisher: Reuters, attributing Russian regulators and WHO
evidence.source_date_semantics: Historical handoff records 2026-10-07T09:06:00Z; not reverified during this review.
evidence.supports: The historical public handoff records Reuters reporting an attributed claim that about 90% of quarantined people had been released.
evidence.does_not_establish: Fresh access to the article, original release records, aligned contact populations and times, or exclusion of transmission.

counter_evidence.title: Current official boundary
counter_evidence.reason: The reviewed official and attributed public statements did not identify the causative agent and reported no established occupational-pathogen link or laboratory accident.

unknowns: Final causative-agent determination and clinical diagnosis
Independent documentation of any occupational pathogen link
Independent documentation of any laboratory accident
Qualifying evidence for a second plague case
Qualifying evidence for a second death
Complete ECDC review, because the targeted source could not be opened during this bounded run
Completion of a fully informed WHO risk assessment based on complete event information

search_provenance.boundary: Four targeted searches and eight page-open attempts; WHO/UN, ECDC, Russian public-health attribution, and reliable original reporting prioritized.
search_provenance.source_types: One international public-health statement, government-attributed reporting, two original news reports, one fact check, one general WHO reference, and one institutional background page. ECDC access remained incomplete.

search_provenance.boundary: Zero new queries and eight targeted reopen attempts; three readable and five inaccessible. This was a source/mapping repair, not a complete news scan.
search_provenance.source_types: Newly readable WHO original statement and attributed public post; a WHO general-reference date correction; retained historical Reuters attribution explicitly marked inaccessible.

search_boundary.public_scope: Final cause, de-identified contact follow-up, WHO/IHR requests, second-employee verification and auditable safety review. Public-health subset only.

history.why: The first public whitelist separated the reported death and official descriptions from unestablished diagnostic and occupational-causation claims; one targeted source path remained inaccessible.
Recovered the public handoff, resolved aliases, added original WHO procedure/risk attribution, and corrected the visible date of the general reference. No clinical conclusion was upgraded.
UNOG displayed publication date corrected from 5 to 6 October. Clinical claim states and evidence-state cutoff unchanged; review incomplete.
Retrieved two Russian press-service attributions as candidates; inaccessible primary records prevent a complete review. Accepted claims, evidence cutoff and evidence-updated timestamp unchanged.
